title: The work cabinet tab strip — two copies of it, and two of its nine tabs
why: The same work cabinet exists in both bundles — `S-024` in `app.html`, `S-091` in `maya-os-site/index.html` — and its nine tabs (`appts|biz|mystat|customers|team|calendar|services|schedule|profile`) overlap almost completely with ASaasOwnerPanel's nine: two implementations of one work cabinet, reached by two different taps of the same bar. It is one of the largest families in the inventory — the two strip rows in this group sit on top of nine further rows carrying the app.html copy's own tabs, eleven of the 101 Maya-owned primary-nav entries the rebuild is meant to collapse, and that is before the cabinet's other shell row and its duplicate Сессии row are counted. The strip is a container and not a capability — the tabs lazy-load on tap and `services` renders exactly one card — but the strip's own code is load-bearing: the fine-grained predicates `saasIsCalManager()` / `saasCalInternal()` / `meAppAccessViewManager()` run where the tab list is built (L13975-13982), and the tap handler beneath it (L13984) is the only place the journal's data is fetched. The strip also manufactures the ambiguity chat-first removes: `calendar` and `schedule` both render the literal label «Расписание» and both appear at once for an internal-calendar manager.
disappear: Both copies of the strip, the tab bar, and the hosting of a business cabinet inside the client `book` screen. All four rows are RETIRE AFTER PARITY — K16, so nothing here is removed at the moment of the merge, only after its target is proven reachable. One thing does not simply fall away with the strip: the tab-keyed bottom-bar mapping (`NAV_BY_SAAS_CAB_TAB = { mystat: 2, profile: 3 }`, L36204). The strip that feeds it goes, but S-091 records that mapping as something the merge must keep resolving, and the two tabs it keys are dispositioned on rows outside this group — so re-keying it is work the merge owes, not a saving it delivers.
remain: The capability behind each tab — but this group names destinations for only three of the nine: `calendar`, `services catalog`, `schedule`. The other six (`appts`, `biz`, `mystat`, `customers`, `team`, `profile`) are dispositioned on their own rows and not here, and they do not all end the same way: `biz` is kept as a fullscreen detail reached by handoff rather than retired, and `profile`/Сессии is retired as UI with the fence kept server-side. This group is therefore not a nine-for-nine parity promise. The tab names must stay resolvable: `?cabinet=<tab>` deep links (allowlist L35674) and the bottom bar both address tabs by name, and that vocabulary survives as intent vocabulary rather than disappearing with the strip. Two capabilities live only in the cabinet copy and are lost by a naive merge into the owner panel: the device/session list with revoke and logout, which has no counterpart in ASaasOwnerPanel's `profile` tab, and `mystat`, the only self-scoped statistics view a plain staff member has. The successors must also carry the visibility rules the tabs carried — the journal under `saasIsCalManager()`, Услуги and Расписание under `saasCalInternal() && saasIsCalManager()` — and `svcCard`'s inline row-editor state `myCalSvcEdit`.
risk: MEDIUM-HIGH — the failure modes here are silent rather than loud. `calendar` is the sole trigger for both `loadMyStaff()` and `loadMyJournal()` (L13984) and the render body re-checks only `myTab` (L14172), so a naive merge leaves the journal unhydrated and without its only client-side gate; `svcCard` is the only consumer of `myCalSvcEdit` (L14351), so a re-parent that drops that state turns per-service editing read-only with no error, and a reordered hydration leaves `svcCard` rendering against a null `myCal`; and because the bottom bar and `?cabinet=` links resolve tabs by name — the post-onboarding redirects emit `onboarded=1&…&cabinet=<tab>` and `cabinet=schedule&calendar_setup=1` (app.html L7196, L7205) — an un-rekeyed merge strands both deep links and the return path out of onboarding. What the merge does not do is close a security hole: the predicates the strip runs are client-side visibility, and today's `?cabinet=` router already admits `calendar`/`services`/`schedule` on the coarse business-role check alone (L35669-35682), without them. It must not be signed as a security improvement either — this group's own approval condition requires the `calendar` gate to be reproduced server-side rather than inherited from the strip, which is the rows' way of saying the server-side equivalent is to be built and proved, not something already evidenced here.
user_impact: Every business user notices, not only an owner or admin-role manager, because two of the four rows (S-024 in app.html, S-091 in maya-os-site/index.html) are the cabinet host itself, not tabs inside it. On the `book` screen today the strip is also a plain master's navigation: `profile`/«Сессии» is pushed unconditionally (app.html L13980) and `mystat` on `saasIsStaffRole() || saasHasStaffProfile()` (L13975), and the bottom bar hard-lands there for a non-manager — «Финансы» → `__meSaasCabinet('mystat', 2)` (L26465), «Клиенты» → `__meSaasCabinet('profile', 3)` (L26476). A client is not entirely untouched either: the `!viewBusiness` branch still paints a one-tab «Записи» strip as the fallback cabinet (L13961-13963). What an owner or cal-manager specifically sees today, and what the re-parenting genuinely fixes, is real and not a generic chat-first benefit: when `saasCalInternal() && saasIsCalManager()` the strip shows two tabs both literally labelled «Расписание» at once — the journal tab (L13976) and the internal-calendar schedule tab (L13979) — an ambiguity that disappears when each is asked for by name. Afterwards, only three of the nine tabs are promised as capabilities (`calendar`, `services catalog`, `schedule`); `appts`, `biz`, `mystat`, `customers`, `team` and `profile` are not named by this group's successor, so "the same content arrives" is not yet true of the surfaces most staff actually use. Two specifics must survive or the content is not the same: the journal is a ±7-day window with a staff filter (L12592-12617), not a day view, and «Услуги» is the price-list EDITOR — svcCard is the only consumer of the inline row state `myCalSvcEdit` (L14351) writing POST/PATCH/DELETE `/internal-calendar/services` (L12641-12669), so a successor that carries the list but not that state turns per-service editing silently read-only. The dossier's own condition still governs: nothing arrives as a widget until the K1 parity harness proves each target reachable from chat.
security_impact: NOT neutral — the two tabs must be split, because only one of them is backstopped server-side. «Услуги» (S-529) is genuinely NEUTRAL: its body re-asserts `saasCalInternal() && saasIsCalManager()` independently of the tab (L14259-14260), and its data is `/internal-calendar/*`, whose controller carries `@TenantScoped()` + `@Roles(TENANT_ADMIN, TENANT_OWNER, BUSINESS_OWNER, ADMINISTRATOR)` (internal-calendar.controller.ts:40-56) — a plain master is refused there, fail-closed. «Расписание»/journal (S-526) is a RISK, and the proposed text gets the direction wrong by attributing it to the same endpoint. The tab predicate is NOT gated on `calendar_source`, and `loadMyJournal` routes to `/integrations/crm/journal` whenever the tenant is external (app.html L12603) — the live MAYA configuration (YClients 503759). That controller's own `@Roles(...CRM_JOURNAL_ROLES)` deliberately admits PROVIDER, EMPLOYEE and STAFF (crm-integration.controller.ts:52-62, 178-179), and `getJournal(tenantId, query)` scopes by tenant only, with no actor scoping (crm.service.ts:3160-3212), while each row carries `client.name` (yclients-crm.adapter.ts:3366-3371). Client-side, `saasIsCalManager()` at L13976 is the ONLY role gate — the journal body tests `myTab !== 'calendar'` and never the role (L14172). So for an external-CRM tenant the removed check is not "already server-side": it is the only place that rule is written, and the server will not refuse the successor. Scale the claim honestly: a plain master already reaches the same endpoint's single-day, all-masters grid through the separate `schedule` screen (ALiveSchedule L30229, L30415; `openDayTile` routes any business role there, L28968-28977), with phones withheld client-side only (`can_see_phone: ssRole() === 'owner'`, L30453). The widening is therefore of degree — the ±7-day range and provider filter — plus the loss of the one expression of the predicate, not a first exposure. Note also that `saasIsCalManager()` admits `manager`, which `INTERNAL_CALENDAR_MANAGER_ROLES` does not, so an internal-calendar manager is painted a tab the server 403s. The host exposure the proposed text found is real and survives: S-024 and S-091 both record that this strip carries the `profile`/«Сессии» device-session list with revoke and logout (L13980-13985, `loadMySessions`), G04's successor names only calendar / services catalog / schedule, and G10's `profile` covers the client profile menus (S-048, S-111, S-176), not this staff device list — so executing the removal as written strands the session-revoke surface with no host. None of these four rows writes or reads a consent record or an audit row, but the journal payload is client ПД, which is exactly why the role predicate has to be carried into the successor rather than assumed server-side. No frozen limitation is contradicted; the reasoning does lean on the same role-gate-as-control framing that "approval is role-gated, NOT separation-of-duties" warns against, and re-keying the back stack, NAV_NO_BAR and NO_PUSH_ROOTS runs into frozen limitation 6 — the shipping frontend is a hand-edited single file with no sources or build script.
